brief.title: When the Wind Turns
brief.premise: A harbour scribe in a monsoon-trade port must reconcile three foreign envoys' rival claims to the first sailing slot before the wind turns and the season is lost.
constraints: Setting is a pre-industrial Indian Ocean trade port; nothing later than the sixteenth century.

world.name: The Monsoon Court
world.description: A great trade port whose whole calendar is set by the monsoon: fleets wait on the wind, sailing slots are worth fortunes, and the harbour court rules who sails first when the wind turns.

locations.name: The Harbour Office
locations.description: The court's counting house where sailing-slot claims are entered in the harbour ledger.

locations.name: The Envoy House
locations.description: The lodging of foreign delegations, where rival claims are argued under the same roof.

locations.name: The Pepper Warehouses
locations.description: The bonded cargo rows where the season's wealth waits on the wind.

locations.name: The Pilot Ghat
locations.description: The harbour steps where the master pilots read the sea and declare the monsoon turned.

factions.name: The Harbour Court
factions.description: The scribes, weighers and slot-keepers who rule the sailing order.

factions.name: The Captains' Majlis
factions.description: The dhow captains' council that bargains for the fleet's slots as one.

factions.name: The Pepper Factors
factions.description: The bonded merchants whose cargo makes the season and whose gifts smooth its way.

rules.statement: No fleet may sail before the pilot ghat declares the monsoon turned.
The first sailing slot belongs to the claim filed earliest in the harbour ledger.
Every gift to a court official is entered in the gift register, or it is a bribe.
An oath sworn over pepper is binding before the harbour court.

history.name: The First Charter
history.description: The sailing slots were created to end the dock riots that met every turning wind.

history.name: The Year of Three Envoys
history.description: Three delegations once deadlocked the court so long that the wind turned around them and the season was lost.

history.name: The Ghat Oath
history.description: After a pilot was bought to misread the sea, the ghat's declarations were bound to public rite.

conflicts.name: The First Slot
conflicts.description: Three envoys claim to have filed in the same hour for the first sailing slot of the monsoon.

conflicts.name: The Unregistered Gifts
conflicts.description: Unregistered gifts have surfaced in the pepper warehouses, implicating the slot-keepers.

characters.name: Deva Anai
characters.description: A junior scribe of the Harbour Office who keeps the slot ledger and can read an hour's filing in the grain of its ink.
characters.motivation: To see the first slot go to whoever filed first, and only them.
characters.goal: Establish the true filing order before the wind turns.
characters.flaw: She believes the ledger is never wrong, which is exactly what the forgers count on.
characters.internal_conflict: Proving a forged filing means accusing the office that raised her.
characters.external_conflict: Three envoys, a factor and half the court want the audit to end inconclusive.

abilities.name: Ledger memory
abilities.description: Recites any entry she has ever copied and detects a hand that is not the clerk's own.

characters.arc: Deva learns a ledger is only as honest as the hand allowed to write it.

characters.name: Suleiman Qadir
characters.description: The richest of the pepper factors, who pre-dated a filing to buy the first slot for a cargo that cannot wait a second turn.
characters.motivation: To sail on the first wind before his cargo's buyers walk away.
characters.goal: Keep the first slot he bought until the monsoon is declared.
characters.flaw: He believes every record has a price because his always did.
characters.internal_conflict: The forged filing saved his season and may cost his name.
characters.external_conflict: Deva's audit can prove his entry was written out of order.

abilities.name: Factor's credit
abilities.description: Borrows against a season not yet sailed and makes creditors wait smiling.

characters.arc: Qadir must choose between the slot that saves his fortune and the name that carries it.

characters.name: Amara
characters.description: The senior pilot of the ghat, whose declaration of the turned wind is the only testimony the court cannot buy.
characters.motivation: To declare the wind honestly and see the fleet sail in the right order.
characters.goal: Settle the filing hour by the only record no one could forge: the sea's.
characters.flaw: She speaks in omen-rite that the court must take on faith.
characters.internal_conflict: Her declaration will end one envoy's season whichever way she calls it.
characters.external_conflict: Every claimant wants her declaration delayed until after their filing stands.

abilities.name: Wind-reading
abilities.description: Reads the turn of the monsoon a day before the sea shows it.

characters.arc: Amara declares the wind on the honest hour and the court must follow.

relationships.description: Amara's declaration can corroborate the true filing hour.
relationships.conflict: Her rite names the hour; Deva's ledger names the claimant.

relationships.description: Deva's ink-reading can prove Qadir's filing was pre-dated.
relationships.conflict: Qadir's gifts to the court make the audit dangerous for her.

storyboard.title: When the Wind Turns
storyboard.logline: A harbour scribe proves which of three envoys truly filed first as the monsoon counts down the season.

scenes.title: Three Envoys, One Hour
scenes.summary: At the Harbour Office, three envoys produce claims filed in the same hour for the first slot; Deva finds one entry's ink laid over another.
scenes.conflict: Two of the three claims cannot both be true.
scenes.outcome: Deva flags the ledger for audit; the court splits.

scenes.title: The Unregistered Gift
scenes.summary: In the Pepper Warehouses, a gift manifests without a register entry, tying Qadir's slot to an unentered favour.
scenes.conflict: An unentered gift is a bribe under the court's own rules.
scenes.outcome: The audit widens from the filings to the office itself.

scenes.title: The Ink Beneath
scenes.summary: Deva audits the slot ledger and finds Qadir's entry written over a filed-and-scraped claim: the first slot was bought with a forged hour.
scenes.conflict: The proof condemns her own office.
scenes.outcome: The scraping is shown to the majlis; the court must rule by the true hour.

scenes.title: The Pilot's Hour
scenes.summary: At the Pilot Ghat, Amara reads the sea and names the true filing hour by the swell that carried each envoy's boat to shore.
scenes.conflict: Her testimony is omen-rite, which the losing envoy will call superstition.
scenes.outcome: The sea's hour matches the scraped claim.

scenes.title: The Ruling
scenes.summary: Before the Envoy House, Deva rules by the scraped claim and the pilot's hour; Qadir confesses rather than let the office burn with him.
scenes.conflict: Qadir's confession costs his season; silence costs his name.
scenes.outcome: The first slot goes to the true filer; the gift register is purged.

scenes.title: The First Sail
scenes.summary: Amara declares the monsoon turned at the ghat, the rightful fleet sails first, and Deva's audit enters the harbour charter.
scenes.conflict: The wind turns once; the ruling must hold when it does.
scenes.outcome: The fleet sails in the honest order; the monsoon court keeps its name.

evidence_summary: The world, cast and storyboard satisfy the brief's pre-industrial monsoon-trade setting; deterministic validators are clean and there are no blocking defects.
